# `hk read`

- **How to hail it:** `hk read`
- **Effect:** read-only (looks, never touches)

Serve hk's Pkl modules to pkl as an external module reader

pkl starts this command to read `hk:` modules, so a config can `amends "hk:/Config.pkl"` and `import "hk:/Builtins.pkl"` and get the modules of the installed hk instead of a pinned package. It speaks Pkl's external reader protocol on stdin and stdout and is not meant to be run by hand. Register it in a PklProject:

    evaluatorSettings {
      externalModuleReaders {
        ["hk"] { executable = "hk"; arguments { "read" } }
      }
    }

or pass `--external-module-reader hk='hk read'` to `pkl eval`.

## Tales from the deck {#examples}

Let pkl and editors read `hk:` modules from the installed hk. pkl starts this command itself.

```sh
pkl eval --external-module-reader 'hk=hk read' hk.pkl
```
